response.justification: Bogdan is an experienced, versatile senior engineer with strong geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and genuine low-latency systems work at Sociomantic (async I/O, fibers, caching, microservices at millions of requests/second). However, the role's primary requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial/open-source settings — is only weakly met: his C/C++ exposure is a ~7-month stint at National Instruments in 2014-2015 plus an academic thesis, with no evidence of C++11+ or Rust. The last decade is predominantly TypeScript/Node.js and D, and there is no routing, tiling, or navigation-guidance experience. He could plausibly ramp given his systems mindset and stated willingness to work across the stack, but he would start behind candidates with current C++/Rust depth, so an interview is only worth it if the team can absorb the ramp-up.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS product experience, including an open-source platform and conference talk
Low-latency, high-throughput distributed backend work (Sociomantic) with async I/O and caching
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, test tooling authorship, Linux and DevOps depth
concerns: Modern C++/Rust experience is minimal and over a decade stale
No routing, tiling, or navigation-guidance pipeline experience
Recent career trajectory is web/full-stack TypeScript, not systems programming
